revisionDesc.change: Vote - AcceptText - This looks convincing. The passage is mentioned by R. Buzón, Die Briefe der Ptolemäerzeit ..., p. 106, as a case of contamination of formulas.

Vote - AcceptText - There are few supplements for the lacuna, and [εὖ] is very likely, not least because the lacuna is very short. Still, the sequence καλῶς ἂν ἔχοι (l. 1) / [εὖ] ἂν ἔχοι (l. 5) before and after the conditional clauses seems a little odd to me. Maybe the repetition of εἰ in l. 4 let the scribe feel the need for a second optative - just maybe.

Submit - The lacuna at the beginning of l. 5 has room for two letters. I propose to restore it as [εὖ] ἂν ἔχοι·, which is well attested in contemporary papyri (see, e.g., P.Cairo Zen. 1 59046, 2-3) My proposal has been entered as <:[εὖ]=PN Alba de Frutos García|ed|[.2]:>
